Pls confirm <@607055410104500244> <@792822129019584562> I think the issue was in capella, we were probably trying to use the v3 endpionts, maybe this is what caused the EL to fall out of sync? ``` Apr 26 10:06:24.123 WARN Error whilst processing payload status error: Api { error: ServerMessage { code: -32602, message: "ExecutionPayloadV2 MUST be used if Shanghai is activated and EIP-4844 is not" } }, service: exec Apr 26 10:06:28.492 WARN Execution engine call failed error: ServerMessage { code: -32602, message: "ExecutionPayloadV2 MUST be used if Shanghai is activated and EIP-4844 is not" }, service: exec Apr 26 10:06:28.492 WARN Error whilst processing payload status error: Api { error: ServerMessage { code: -32602, message: "ExecutionPayloadV2 MUST be used if Shanghai is activated and EIP-4844 is not" } }, service: exec ``` what payload version do you use between capella and deneb? I think wiping it should fix the issue but we'll still have to figure it out for next time it should be v2, and then switch to v3 from deneb fork? ok wiping now Pretty sure the other LH node also out of sync btw probably similar issue. I'll check that out too wouldn't same issue occur again? restarting it now, pls keep an eye on the logs I guess it depends on if we are *in* deneb at that point are v3 endpoints enabled in ethereum js? i think endpoints usage is evaluated on basis of payload's timestamp we had the same point of confusion for capella but the el endpoints are spec'd out as backwards compatible we'll always try to use latest looks like LH - ethereumjs synced to head the spec says always try the latest available? ``` engine_newPayloadV3 Request method: engine_newPayloadV3 params: ExecutionPayloadV1 | ExecutionPayloadV2 | ExecutionPayloadV3, where: ExecutionPayloadV1 MUST be used if the timestamp value is lower than the Shanghai timestamp, ExecutionPayloadV2 MUST be used if the timestamp value is greater or equal to the Shanghai and lower than the EIP-4844 activation timestamp, ExecutionPayloadV3 MUST be used if the timestamp value is greater or equal to the EIP-4844 activation timestamp, Client software MUST return -32602: Invalid params error if the wrong version of the structure is used in the method call. ``` i will have to see since ethereumjs<>lighthouse has synced what the real logic is behind the validations yes so its based on timestamp (so basically slot) of the payload Is it possible ethjs was able to sync EL blocks via p2p so we never had to go through the API for old blocks? yes you are correct, ethereumjs did backfill/beacon sync If I read this spec correctl
